## dependency_form

- The one prerequisite sentence stands verbatim, state form, in the blocked policy's hub; it is not restated as an action and no resolving tool or problem is named beside it.
- Policy-side note (source class: non-prerequisite rule sentence naming another problem's write): further_extension_worksheet (the grant's computation document) says "…so a request re-filed on the day of the request it replaces is the one a grant rests on", and the depended-on hub extension_request_refiling_terms says the earlier request "stays on file, while any grant rests on the most recently received request awaiting a decision" (status table: "the request a grant rests on | … which is the re-filed request"). Both are the source's own rule text — maturity_ext_further_extension_sizing.rule "…so that a request re-filed on the day of the request it replaces is the one a grant rests on" and maturity_ext_further_extension_ask.rule "…while any grant rests on the most recently received request awaiting a decision". The rendering adds no tool name, route or order beyond them. In the blind audit the hop was still derived state-derived from the prerequisite sentence plus the re-filing rule, and the same-day clause was not needed (the re-filing is two days after the pending request). It is recorded here because it is the one place in the corpus where the grant's documents name the depended-on write; the coordinator may route it to the policy side. Not a KB verdict.
- No aggregated chain, route, ordered step list, chain-walking example, task-mirroring title or opening (titles: "Re-Filing an Extension Request with Current Evidence", "Further Extensions of a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Case" — general subjects); factor docs neither assign a tier nor point at a worksheet or another factor; worksheets carry no hint of variation beyond the source's own "As standard" wording.

**PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT RED).
